Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Financial literacy is developed as the learner acquires knowledge on trade and use of advertisements to increase sales. Links to other learning areas: The learner is able to relate the concept of trade and advertisement to the content learnt in Social Studies.

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 5.3.1: Functional writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) highlight the format of a shopping list, b) write a shopping list for life-long SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  work collaboratively to search for varied samples of shopping lists from print and non-print sources,  write down the components of a shopping list,  describe things to be bought using aspects such as colour, amount, material, shape, size (adjectives) KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is a shopping list important? learning, c) enjoy personal writing for communication.  work jointly with peers to write a shopping list for an event based on the theme  present the shopping list in class for peer review  organize the shopping lists in the class portfolio for reference. Core Competences to be developed  Communication is enhances as the learner uses developed shopping lists in the market to pass their requests to shopkeepers.  Self- efficacy is developed as the learner confidently presents his shopping lists for peer review. Values:  Integrity is developed as the learner acquires the knowledge of using shopping lists to budget for their money.  Love is enhanced as the learner appreciates and gives positive comments to peers during review session. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Financial literacy is enhanced as the learner is able to appreciate the importance of preparing shopping lists before going to purchase. Links to other learning areas: The learner is able to relate the concept of shopping lists to their learning in mathematics.

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 6.1.1 Listening for information. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify special and vulnerable groups from a listening comprehension for information, b) use vocabulary based on the theme in conversations for communication, c) appreciate vocabulary acquisition in language development. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to a listening comprehension from the teacher and identify vocabulary related to the theme,  read words aloud and identify verbs,  view pictures in books and identify vocabulary,  mimic and say vocabulary in cards accurately with peers,  collaborate with peers to discuss the meaning of vocabulary,  create sentences using vocabulary and read them aloud,  search for vocabulary related to the theme online and create vocabulary charts,  narrate stories containing vocabulary related to the theme with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we get meaning of words? 2. What is the importance of vocabulary in communication? Core Competencies to be developed:  Communication and collaboration is developed as learners listen to texts, discuss vocabulary and narrate stories based on the theme.  Digital literacy is promoted as the learner uses technology to search for vocabulary related to the theme. Values:  Responsibility is acquired as the learner takes different roles during general class activities.  Social justice is enhanced as the learner is exposed to content about special and vulnerable groups in society. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Human rights education is promoted as the learner is exposed to content on issues of concern to special and vulnerable groups; and take initiative to cultivate social justice. Link to other learning areas: The learner is able to relate the content on special and vulnerable groups to the teachings in Religious Education.

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 6.2.1Reading fluency. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) predict events in a text bases on the theme for comprehension, b) skim and scan texts based on the theme for general information, c) appreciate skimming and SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  observe pictures and identify action words(verbs),  Predict texts based on the title or picture clues,  practice skimming and scanning texts for specific details collaboratively,  practice reading texts clearly and fluently and give peer reviews,  read texts and answer comprehension questions,  brain storm skimming and scanning strategies with peers,  use digital devices to find information on KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we skim and scan text? scanning in reading a variety of texts. skimming and scanning,  recite a poem based on the theme fluently using expressions. Core Competences to be developed:  Communication is promoted as the learner skims and scans through a text for pick out specific details and information with ease.  Self-efficacy is promoted as the learner confidently recites poems fluently and with expressions. Values:  Responsibility is cultivated as the learner uses the digital devices appropriately and for the right purpose.  Respect is portrayed as the learner accommodates divergent opinion as they brainstorm on skimming and scanning strategies. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Digital literacy is enhanced as the learner manipulates and uses technology devices to search for information about skimming and scanning strategies. Links to Other learning areas: The learner is able to apply the skimming and scanning strategies acquired to their reading activities in English and Kiswahili.

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 6.3.1 Creative writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify idioms commonly used in the locality for SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learners is guided to:  mention idioms commonly used in the locality with peers  listen to an audio recording on a creative story, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why are idioms important? information, b) use idioms commonly used in the locality to write an imaginative story, c) Enjoy using idioms from their locality in writing.  list idioms from the audio story,  discuss the meaning of various idioms used in the locality,  use idioms from the locality to write creative stories collaboratively,  read their creative stories in class for peer review, Core Competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration is enhanced as the learner shares their ideas and opinion on meanings of various idioms.  Creativity and imagination is cultivated as the learner uses idioms to write own creative stories. Values:  Respect is enhanced as the learner accommodates peers as they work together despite their physical and cultural background differences.  Honesty is enhanced as the learner gives honest opinion as they read the creative stories in class for peer review. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Social cohesion is enhanced as the learners accommodates in their life’s special and vulnerable groups of people. Links to Other learning areas: The learner is able to relate and connect their learning of idioms to Kiswahili and English languages.

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 7.1.1Making opinions and judgements. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify interjections accurately in a conversation for comprehension, b) apply turn taking and interrupting politely in a conversation, c) advocate for good interrupting and turn taking skills in conversations. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  view and watch recorded clips and identify components of a conversation,  role play using introductory and closing phrases in a conversation with peers,  pick out interjections in an oral conversation in class,  participate in a dialogue about the theme while using interjection and turn taking skills,  compose and sing a song about talents,  discuss about the theme while applying appropriate skills for a conversation collaboratively, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you respond or ask questions during conversations? 2. Why is it important to take turns and interject appropriately in conversations? Core Competencies to be developed:  Self-efficacy is promoted as the learner role plays, sings and discusses the theme confidently.  Learning to learn is developed as the learner practices using interjections and taking turns in varied conversations settings. Values:  Unity is enhanced as the learner harmoniously watches videos and discuss the theme with peers.  Love is developed as the learners and peers discover their different talents and appreciate their diverse potential. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues: Peer education and mentorship is promoted as the learner is able to link their talents and abilities to future careers and occupations. Link to other learning areas: The learner is able to link and apply two-way conversation skills in their learning of Kiswahili and English languages.

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 7.2.1Reading comprehension. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) read stories fluently and with expression for comprehension, b) answer comprehension question based on the theme, c) enjoy reading texts for comprehension. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read short stories on animals and answer comprehension questions,  read poems and identify the message  discuss characters and themes in stories collaboratively,  read and discuss the moral lessons in the short stories  pick out interjections from simple texts,  role play different characters in stories with peers,  use dictionary to search for meaning of vocabulary. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we identify characters in a story? 2. What moral lesson can we learn from a story? Core Competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration as is promoted as the learner reads stories and comprehend the moral lessons collaboratively.  Problem solving skill is developed as the learner identifies characters and moral lessons in stories. Values:  Respect is enhanced as the learner role play and appreciates the different character roles in a story.  Responsibility is inculcated as the learners draws and applies moral lessons from stories in their day-to-day living. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Career progression and development is enhanced as the learner is able to link their talents to future occupations in the society. Links to other subjects: The learner is able to apply the skills of drawing moral lessons from the story to their interpretation of teachings in Religious Studies.

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 7.3.1 Creative writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand the learner should be able to: a) highlight features of a poem, b) write a simple poem using neat and legible handwriting for communication, c) appreciate written poetry for self- expression. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to audio recording on simple poems,  identify features of a poem from the audio recording,  compose and write simple poems based on the theme using a neat and legible handwriting,  recite the poems fluently and do a peer review collaboratively,  record their poem recitations using digital devices,  write a paragraph of a story and punctuate appropriately. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why write legibly and neatly? Core Competences to be developed:  Communication is enhanced as the learner listens to an audio recording and identify features of a poem.  Creativity and imagination is cultivated as the learner composes and writes poems in neat and legible handwriting. Values:  Unity is enhanced as the learner works harmoniously with peers to create simple poems based on the theme.  Respect is promoted as the learner accommodates opinion given by others during peer review sessions. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Digital literacy is promoted as the learner manipulates digital devices to record themselves reciting poems. Links to Other Subjects: The learner is able to relate the concept of talents to the learning in Religious Education.

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 8.1.1 Expressing personal opinions. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) speak clearly and audibly on a topic to express personal opinions effectively, b) apply audience awareness skills in public speaking, c) appreciate public speaking skills for self-expression. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  organise ideas on a topic and present audibly and in good sound projection,  discuss with peers audience awareness skills for presentations,  use words and their opposites in sentences correctly,  record themselves performing speeches and share in class,  take part in a public speaking competition on a topic,  imitate public speeches and presentations clearly and accurately,  watch popular public speeches on care for digital devices and discuss with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do we consider when speaking in public? 2. Why is it important to speak clearly and audibly? 3. How do we express personal opinions clearly Core Competencies to be developed:  Self-efficacy is acquired as the learner organises ideas and make public speeches effectively and efficiently.  Creativity and imagination is developed as the learner explores topics and take part in a public speaking competition with peers. Values:  Unity is promoted as the learner collaborates with peers to organise ideas on a topic for presentation in class.  Love is cultivated as the learner discovers varied ways of caring for digital devices. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Self-management and awareness is enhanced as the learner discovers and applies public speaking skills in their communication. Link to other learning areas:

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 8.2.1 Extensive Reading. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) outline the characters in the narrative for comprehension, b) retell the flow of the events in the story for expression, c) appreciate the moral lesson from stories for lifelong learning. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  collect a variety of narratives in the community,  read level readers individually and make notes or summaries,  read texts based on the theme and identify vocabulary,  find meaning of vocabulary from context,  use dictionary to confirm meaning of vocabulary from texts,  respond to comprehension questions from level readers,  discuss lessons learnt from level readers,  visit a library to select a material for individual reading. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What should you consider when reading silently? 2. How do you keep a record of learnt vocabulary? Core Competences to be developed:  Learning to learn is enhanced as the learner search for meaning of vocabulary from contexts and in the dictionary.  Critical thinking and problem solving is cultivated as the learner confidently writes summaries of texts read. Values:  Responsibility is nurtures as the learner keeps records of summaries of the materials read.  Unity is promoted as the learner bonds well with peers and community as they collect narratives. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): The knowledge on care for digital devices is enhanced as the learner reads and interacts with content on the theme. Links to other learning areas: The learner is able to relate and apply dictionary skills in their learning of vocabulary in English and Kiswahili languages.

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 8.3.1 Functional writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the components of a friendly letter for comprehension, b) write a friendly letter based on the theme for expression, c) Enjoy writing friendly letters for communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  work collaboratively to collect samples of friendly letters from print and non- print sources,  identify components of a friendly letter,  discuss with peers the various components of sample friendly letters,  compose a friendly letter and type in a digital device,  proofread their friendly letters and make corrections,  read and share friendly letters through social medial and emails. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why write friendly letters? Core Competences to be developed:  Creativity and imagination is enhanced as learners use a digital device to write a friendly letter based on the theme.  Learning to learn is developed as learners are being exposed to the concept of friendly letter writing for life-long learning. Values:  Responsibility is nurtured as the learner takes initiative to care for digital devices and use them appropriately.  Love is promoted as the learner sends messages to peers suing friendly letters. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Digital literacy is promoted as the learner appreciate and takes responsibility to care for digital devices.

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 9.1.1 Language strategies on daily experiences. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe national events fluently and with expression, b) compose songs based on patriotism for expression, c) value the place of national days in promoting ethnic cohesion. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to recorded events on national days,  work collaboratively to build a vocabulary bank on words based on national days,  describe the events fluently, with accuracy and with expression (adverbs),  listen to each other describing events and identify adverbs used,  work collaboratively to compose patriotic songs for a national day,  perform the patriotism songs during an interclass festival. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do we celebrate national days? 2. How can we describe an event interestingly? Core Competencies to be developed:  Citizenship is enhanced as the learner work collaboratively with peers to compose patriotic songs to show love for their country.  Communication is developed as the learner describes national events and sing to pass messages on national days. Values:  Unity is acquired as the learner uses songs to preach social cohesion in the country.  Patriotism is enhanced as the learner performs the patriotic songs during festivals to show love for their country. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues: Ethnic and positive racial relations is enhanced as the learner is exposed to content on patriotism and nationalism. Link to other learning areas The learner is able to relate the concept nationalism and patriotism to their learning in Social Studies.

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) read a story based on the theme for comprehension, b) make predictions on the events of the story, c) answer comprehension questions correctly, d) enjoy reading texts for comprehension. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  select a reading material based on the theme,  predict and preview text based on the theme,  read simple passages on national days and answer questions collaboratively,  elicit topical words from passages on national days and infer the meaning from context,  discuss events in the stories read with peers,  use digital devices to find texts for reading and make notes. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why make predictions in stories? Core Competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration is promoted as the leaner finds and discusses meaning of new words collaboratively.  Digital literacy is developed as the learner uses digital devices to search for information on national days. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Self-esteem is enhanced as he learner confidently reads passages and discusses events in the stories for comprehensions. Values:  Love is nurtures as the learner interacts with reading materials on nationalism.  Unity is cultivated as the learner is able to cooperate with peers as they work together. Links to other subjects: Languages teach reading to infer meaning from context while social studies teaches national days.

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 9.3.1 Functional writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) identify components of a recipe for information, b) write a recipe of their favourite food for instruction, c) enjoy writing recipes of various foods for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  make a list of adverbs based on the theme,  role play various adverbs based on the theme with peers,  identify adverbs and write them on flashcards,  discus different components of recipes with peers,  collaborate to write a recipe on a common cultural food from their community,  share their recipes with other groups in class,  pin the recipes on the classroom gallery for a gallery walk, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you write clear instructions? Core Competences to be developed:  Creativity and imagination is enhanced as the learner composes and organises ideas to write a recipe on a common cultural food. Values:  Unity is achieved as the learner works with peers to write a recipe on a common cultural food from their community.  Love is cultivated as the learner share positive feedback on recipes with other classmates. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Cultural awareness is enhanced as the learner is exposed to recipes on different cultural foods. Links to Other Subjects: The learner is able to relate and apply the concept of recipe writing to the learning of method of food preparation in Integrated Science.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Selected Surah: - Al-Kauthar - Al-Maun - Al-Quraysh - Al-Fil
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 QUR’AN. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Selected Surah: - Al-Kauthar - Al-Maun - Al-Quraysh - Al-Fil (16 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read and memorise the selected surahs for spiritual nourishment, b) outline the basic meaning of the selected surahs, c) deduce lessons from the selected surah , d) appreciate the Qur’an as the first source of guidance. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to the teacher/resource person/digital device on the recitation of the selected surah,  recite the selected surahs after the teacher/peer/or the digital devices,  read the selected surahs from a digital device/mus- haf/charts,  practice pronunciation through listening to digital devices,  recite the selected surahs severally to enhance memorization,  listen to the basic meaning of the selected surahs from digital devices and make anecdotal notes,  discuss the different ways of applying the teachings and lessons learnt from the selected surahs. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to recite the Qur’an? 2. What lessons do we learn from the selected surah? Core competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration: is enhance through contributing to group decision making while discussing on ways of applying the teachings of the selected surah  Critical thinking and problem solving: is enhanced through application of the teachings drawn from the selected surah. Values:  Responsibility: hard work is inculcated as learners recite selected surah severally to enhance memorization PCIs:  Self-esteem: as learners discuss the different ways of applying the teachings and lessons learnt from the selected surahs Links to other subjects:

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Hadith. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Hadith on good Behaviour ( 3 Lessons ). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify examples of good behaviour from the selected Hadith for character building, b) discuss the significance of the selected Hadith in shaping the character of a Muslim, c) appreciate the teachings of the Hadith by applying them in day to day life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: Read the following Hadith on good behaviour:  read from chart/digital devices the Hadith on good behaviour:  “Fear Allah wherever you are and follow up a bad deed with a good deed, it will wipe it out. And behave well towards other people.” (Al-Tirmidhi).  identify good behaviour mentioned in the Hadith and present in plenary ,  discuss the teachings and relevance of the Hadith in their daily life,  role play acts showing good behaviour mentioned in the Hadith. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should one behave well? 2. What actions show that you fear Allah? Core competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration :through group discussion on the teachings and relevance of the Hadith on good behaviour  Learning to learn: by extending the teachings to new situations. Values: Respect acceptance and appreciating diverse opinions through group discussion on the teachings and relevance of the Hadith in their daily life. PCIs:  skills of knowing and living with others  Self-esteem skills of knowing and living with self.  Social cohesion by treating others well. Links to other subjects: Languages- Arabic, English as they read and explain the meaning of the Hadith

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Hadith. SUB-STRAND: 2.2 Hadith on Greetings (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the importance of Islamic greetings in the life of a Muslim, b) practise Islamic greetings to promote love and unity in the society, c) appreciate the use of Islamic greetings in bringing harmony in the society. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: read the following Hadith on greetings: “…. Shall I inform you of something which, if you do, you will love one another? Promote greetings (salaam) amongst yourselves.” (Muslim)  Watch/listen to Islamic greetings from digital devices,  demonstrate Islamic greetings in pairs,  discuss the importance of Islamic greetings in the life of a Muslim and make summary notes,  search online and sing Qasida on Islamic greetings,  practise Islamic greetings to promote love and unity as learners come to class/school. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should a Muslim use Islamic greetings? Core competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration: through group discussion on the importance of Islamic greetings  Digital literacy: as learners search online to access qasida to watch/ listen and sing on Islamic greetings. Values: Love is enhance as they demonstrate Islamic greetings in pairs frienship is developed PCIs: social cohesion through the practise of Islamic greetings to promote love and unity as learners come to class/school. Links to other subjects: Creative as learners listen and sing Qasida on Islamic greetings

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Hadith. SUB-STRAND: 2.3 Hadith on Knowledge (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read the Hadith as a source of reference in seeking knowledge, b) explain the importance of seeking knowledge for the benefit of this world and the Hereafter, c) appreciate the teachings of the Hadith by working hard in school. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  Read from a chart/digital devices the Hadith on knowledge:  “Seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim.” (Al- Tirmidhi).  Search online the importance of seeking knowledge and present it in class,  discuss ways of improving academic performance in school,  role play acts on the importance of seeking knowledge in the Muslim society. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to seek knowledge in Islam? 2. What challenges may hinder one from acquiring education? Core competences to be developed:  Critical thinking and problem solving: as learner proactively discuss on ways of improving academic performance in their school  Digital literacy: as leaners search online for information on the importance of seeking knowledge to a accomplish the task Values: Responsibility as learner engages in assigned roles and duties while role playing on acts importance of seeking knowledge as a Muslim. PCIs: Citizenship: Human rights and responsibility as learner role play acts on the importance of seeking knowledge as Muslim Links to other subjects: Languages as they acquire reading skills through reading the Hadith.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Hadith. SUB-STRAND: 2.4 Hadith on Responsible living (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline five issues that mankind should account for according to the Hadith, b) describe the lessons learnt from the Hadith , c) appreciate the teachings of the Hadith by living responsibly. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learners are guided to:  Read from a chart/digital device the Hadith on responsible living: “The son of Adam will not be dismissed from Allah on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about five issues: his life and how he lived it, his youth and how he used it, his wealth and how he earned and spent it, and how he acted on his knowledge.” (Al-Tirmithi)  outline the five issues that mankind must account for on the Day of Resurrection,  describe the lessons learnt from the Hadith and do class resentations,  dramatize ways of living responsibly,  role play ways of earning lawful income and spending. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can the youth live responsibly? 2. How can knowledge be used to benefit others? Core competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration: through group discussion on the five issues that mankind must account for on the Day of Resurrection,  Critical thinking and problem solving: through dramatization of ways of living responsibly Values: Unity as learners strive to achieve common goal in dramatizing ways of living responsibly PCIs: Financial literacy: as learners role play ways of earning lawful income and spending wealth. Links to other subjects: Social Studies ethical ways of generation income

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Belief in Allah 3.1.1 Attributes of Allah: - Al- Ghaffaar (The Forgiver) - Al-Alim (The All Knowing) - Al-Hafeedh (The Protector) - Al-Hakam (The Judge) - Al-Hayu (The Ever Living) - Al-Waahid (The One) (6 Lessons )
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Pillars of Iman. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Belief in Allah 3.1.1 Attributes of Allah: - Al- Ghaffaar (The Forgiver) - Al-Alim (The All Knowing) - Al-Hafeedh (The Protector) - Al-Hakam (The Judge) - Al-Hayu (The Ever Living) - Al-Waahid (The One) (6 Lessons ). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline the attributes of Allah and their corresponding meaning, b) explain the importance of the attributes of Allah, c) use the attributes of Allah while making dua (supplication), d) appreciate the unique attributes of Allah as part of Islamic faith. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner guided to:  listen to the recitation of the attributes of Allah from a digital device,  match the attributes of Allah with corresponding meaning using flash cards,  discuss the importance of the attributes of Allah and make notes,  use the attributes of Allah while making dua,  sing qasida on the attributes of Allah,  match the Atributes with meaning using flash cards. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What lessons are learnt from the attributes of Allah? 2. Why should one use the attributes of Allah while making dua (supplications)? Core competences to be developed:  Creativity and imagination: as learner match the attributes of Allah with corresponding meaning using flash cards. Values: Love as learners work in groups, share materials and information. PCIs: Self-esteem when matching the attributes of Allah with their meaning. Links to other subjects: Creative –as learner sing qasida using attributes of Allah

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2 Belief in angels 3.2.1 Characteristics of angels (3 Lessons )
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Pillars of Iman. SUB-STRAND: 3.2 Belief in angels 3.2.1 Characteristics of angels (3 Lessons ). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) state the characteristics of angels to strengthen their iman, b) explain the significance of the belief in angels in the life of a Muslim, c) obey Allah’s commands by emulating angels, d) differentiate between angels and human beings to appreciate Allah’s creation, e) appreciate the belief in angels as a pillar of iman. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  search for information on the characteristics of angels from digital devices/books/resource persons and present in class,  brainstorm on the significance of belief in angels and make notes,  role play different situations that depict obedience to Allah’s commands (obeying parents, teachers, elders, school rules),  read a verse from the Qur’an on the obedience of angels on Allah’s commands (Q66: 6). KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What is the significance of believing in angels? 2. How can Muslims show obedience to Allah? Core competences to be developed: Communication and collaboration: through group discussion on the significance of belief in angels Creativity and imagination: as learners role play different situations that depict obedience to Allah’s commands Values: Responsibility as learners take roles play different situations that depict obedience to Allah’s commands PCIs: Positive discipline as learners obey the commands of Allah Links to other subjects:As the learner role play different situations that depict obedience to Allah’s commands (obeying parents, teachers, elders, school rules)is able to social institutions in Social studies

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3 Belief in Prophets 3.3.1 Qualities of Prophets
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Pillars of Iman. SUB-STRAND: 3.3 Belief in Prophets 3.3.1 Qualities of Prophets (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the qualities of Prophets for character formation, b) apply values learnt from the qualities of Prophets in their daily lives, c) appreciate belief in Allah’s Prophets by emulating the qualities of Prophets. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  search for information on the qualities of Prophets from digital, devices/books/resource persons and display in class,  narrate a story of any Prophet that shows these qualities,  role play situations that demonstrate values learnt from the qualities of the Prophets e.g.(honesty, obedience ,patience),  discuss how the qualities of the Prophets learnt can be applied in school situation. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can qualities of the Prophets be applied in daily life? 2. Why are Prophets regarded as role models? Core competences to be developed:  Self-efficacy: through narrating the stories of the Prophets and emulating them  Creativity and imagination: through role play situations that demonstrate values learnt from the qualities of the Prophets Values: Integrity as leaners emulate and role play situations that demonstrate values learnt from the qualities of the Prophets PCIs: Self-esteem learners emulate and role play situations that demonstrate values learnt from the qualities of the Prophets Links to other subjects: as the learner role play rsituations that demonstrate values learnt from the qualities of the Prophets e.g.(honesty, obedience ,patience) is able relate to values in social studies

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3.2 Miracles of Prophets - Nuh (A.S) - Musa (A.S) - Issa (A.S.)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Pillars of Iman. SUB-STRAND: 3.3.2 Miracles of Prophets - Nuh (A.S) - Musa (A.S) - Issa (A.S.) (6 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the miracles perfomed by the selected Prophets to strengthen their iman (faith), b) discuss lessons learnt from the miracles of the selected Prophets, c) appreciate the miracles of the selected Prophets to build their reliance on Allah. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch/listen to stories of the miracles of the selected Prophets from digital devices and make notes.  deduce lessons from the miracles of the selected Prophets and present in class,  Match the name of the Prophets with miracles performed using flash cards,  draw, colour and display items related to the miracles of the selected Prophet. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What is a miracle? 2. Why did Prophets perform miracles? Core competences to be developed:  Critical thinking and problem solving: through deduce lessons from the miracles of the selected Prophets and present in class  Creativity and imagination: through draw, colour and display items related to the miracles of the selected Prophet Values: Respect as leaners work together and share materials during class activities PCIs: -Self-esteem through narration of the miracles Links to other subjects: Creative Arts as they draw and colour different items. Core competences to be developed:  Creativity and imagination: is enhanced while roleplaying the nullifiers of swalah in class PCIs: Health- personal hygiene as learners maintain cleanliness for prayers

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2 Sunnah (Optional) Prayers: 4.2.1 Qabliyah and Ba'diyah ( 3 Lessons)
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Devotional Acts. SUB-STRAND: 4.2 Sunnah (Optional) Prayers: 4.2.1 Qabliyah and Ba'diyah ( 3 Lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the significance of performing sunnah prayers in the life of a Muslim, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  discuss sunnah prayers performed before and after fardh prayers and display in class using charts, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should a Muslim perform Qabliya and ba’diyah? b) perform Qabliyah and Ba’diyah prayers to earn rewards from Allah, c) appreciate the performance of Qabliyah and Ba’diyah to emulate the sunnah of the Prophet (S.A.W.).  match/fill gaps using digital devices/charts/pocket boards the number of raakat for Qabliyah and ba’diyah for each fardh prayer,  brainstorm on the importance of observing qabliyah and ba’diyah and write notes,  perform Qabliyah and ba’diyah prayers. Core competences to be developed:  Digital literacy: through matching/filling in gaps by using digital devices,  Communication and collaboration: through group discussion on sunnah prayers performed before and after fardh prayers while writing them on a chart Values: Unity as learners discuss sunnah prayers performed before and after fardh prayers and display in class using charts PCIs: Life skills –Tolerance during discussion and respecting others opinion in group work Links to other subjects: as the learner counts the number of Qabliya and ba’diyah in each of the fardh prayers and their total in a day and relate the concept of addition

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Devotional Acts. SUB-STRAND: 4.2.2 Taraweh and Witr (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the significance of performing Taraweh and witr prayers in the life of a Muslim, b) Perform swalatul Taraweh and Witr for spiritual nourishment, c) Appreciate the performance of Taraweh and witr prayers to earn thawab, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch a video on the performance of swalatul Taraweh and witr through digital devices and discuss the procedure of performing the prayer,  Demonstrate/role play swalatul Taraweh and witr in class,  discuss the importance of performing swalatul Taraweh and witr and present in class, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What is the significance of praying swalatul Taraweh and witr? d) develop a habit of performing Taraweh and witr prayers to earn blessing of Allah.  Keep personal logs for a week on how they perform Taraweh/witr prayers. Core competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration: through group discussion on the importance of performing swalatul taraweh and witr,  Creativity and imagination : while role playing swalatul Taraweh and witr in class Values: Responsibility as learners take roles to demonstrate swalatul Taraweh and witr in class PCIs: Self-esteem when demonstrate swalatul Taraweh and witr in class Links to other subjects: As the learner demonstrate swalatul Taraweh and witr is able to relate to concept of even and odd number

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Devotional Acts. SUB-STRAND: 4.3 Swadaqah (Charity) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify forms of swadaqah for character development, b) demontrate different acts of swadaqah to earn rewards, c) explain the benefits of practising acts of swadaqah in the society, d) appreciate the different forms of swadaqah in their daily life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  get pictures from digital devices/print media on forms of swadaqah and display them in class  discuss the different forms of swadaqah in pairs/group as per the teachings of the Prophet (s.a.w) (e.g. feeding an animal, removing an obstacle from the path, sharing with others etc.),  participate in charitable activities (clean up exercise, visit to children’s home, tree planting…),  discuss the benefits of giving charity in pairs/group and do class presentation. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What acts of swadaqah do Muslims perform? 2. What are the benefits of practising swadaqah? Core competences to be developed: Communication and collaboration: through group discussion on the benefits of giving charity in pairs/group and making class presentation, Creativity and imagination: as they get pictures from digital devices/print media on forms of swadaqah and display them in class Values: Responsibility is enhanced as learner get pictures from digital devices/print media on forms of swadaqah and display them in class Links to other subjects: Creative Arts as learner get pictures from digital devices/print media on forms of swadaqah and display them in class Core competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration: through group discussion on the conditions for saum and making class presentation Values: Respect as is inculcated during group discussion through appreciating diverse opinions PCIs: Social cohesion through the application of the virtue of generosity

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Devotional Acts. SUB-STRAND: 4.4.3 Nullifiers of Saum (fasting) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the nullifiers of saum to safeguard the validity of saum, b) practce suam as pillar of Islam , c) appreciate fasting as a means of gaining taqwa (piety). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  discuss in pairs/group the nullifiers of saum and make oral presentation in class,  sort nullifiers of saum from of conditions on flash cards, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should Muslims observe rules and regulation when fasting? 2. What virtues do Muslims learn from fasting? Core competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration: through group discussion on the nullifiers of saum and making oral presentation in class Values: Respect is inculcated during group discussion as learners appreciating diverse opinions PCIs: Empathy as leaners observe saum by thinking about the learners/people who don’t have food. Links to other subjects:

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Values). SUB-STRAND: 5.1 Virtues 5.1.1 Sabr (Patience) ( 2 Lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the importance of exhibiting patience in their daily life, b) practise patience as a virtue for character formation, c) appreciate the virtue of patience as a means of earning rewards from Allah. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learners is guided to:  narrate short stories portraying patience,  watch/listen to a story on patience and deduce the teachings,  discuss in pairs/group the importance of observing patience,  participate in activities that involve practising patience e.g.turn taking during games, when queueing  role play activities that encourage/show patience. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should a Muslim observe patience? 2. When should a Muslim practise patience? Core competences to be developed:  Creativity and imagination: as learners narrate short stories portraying patience  Communication and collaboration: through group discussion on the importance of observing patience. Values: Respect by tolerance during group discussion on the importance of patience by appreciating diverse opinions PCIs: Tolerance during group discussion on the importance of patience by appreciating diverse opinions Links to other subjects:

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Values). SUB-STRAND: 5.2 Effects of Social Media ( 2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the positive and negative effects of social media on the youth SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  debate on the positive and negative effects of social media KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can one use social media positively? 2. How can social media enhance learning? b) outline ways of using social media to facilitate learning c) use social media responsibly to benefit self and others.  discuss in pairs/group how to use social media responsibly and present in class  demonstrate how to use social media to facilitate learning Core competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration: through debate on the positive and negative effects of social media  Creativity and imagination: as learners demonstrate how to use social media to facilitate learning Values: Responsibility as they learners take different roles in demonstrate how to use social media to facilitate learning PCIs: Self-esteem through positive use of social media. Links to other subjects: Science and technology as they cover content of social media.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.3 Prohibitions in Islam (Vices) 5.3.1 Evils of Gambling ( 2 lessons)
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Values). SUB-STRAND: 5.3 Prohibitions in Islam (Vices) 5.3.1 Evils of Gambling ( 2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the evils of gambling to promote responsible citizenship, b) state ways of discouraging gambling in the society, c) appreciate the prohibition of gambling by working hard for halaal (legal) earning. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  discuss in pairs/group the effects of gambling and present in class (loss of property, family break down),  role play the effects of gambling,  brainstorm on ways of discouraging gambling in the society and display on a chart . KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What are the effects of participating in gambling? 2. Why is gambling forbidden in Islam? Core competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration: through group discussion on the effects of gambling and present in class Values: Patriotism as learners brainstorm on ways of discouraging gambling in the society and display a chart on the same. PCIs: Financial literacy as learners discuss the effects of gambling and present in class Links to other subjects: social studies cover content on citizenship

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.4 Dua (Supplications) 5.4.1 Dua On Increase In Knowledge ( 3 Lessons)
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Values). SUB-STRAND: 5.4 Dua (Supplications) 5.4.1 Dua On Increase In Knowledge ( 3 Lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) memorise the selecteddua as a form of ibadah, b) apply the dua (supplication ) in day to day life, c) explain the importance of the dua to a person seeking knowledge, d) appreciate the act of supplication as a form of Ibadah (act of worship). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen and recite the following dua from a digital device/teacher,  “Oh Allah make what you teach me beneficial, teach me what is beneficial, and increase me in knowledge.”  recite the dua every morning before start of class,  brainstorm on the importance of making dua and write notes. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What is the importance of making dua always? Values: Respect for others and appreciating diverse opinions during brainstorming on the importance of dua PCIs: Self-esteem through recite the dua every morning before start of class

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.0 Muamalat (Social Relations). SUB-STRAND: 6.1 Etiquette of Islamic Wedding Celebrations (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe the etiquette to be observed during Islamic wedding celebrations, b) outline unislamic activities that take place during wedding celebrations, c) appreciate Islamic wedding celebrations as part of Islamic heritage. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  brainstorm on a wedding celebration they have attended and note down what they observed/experienced,  watch an Islamic wedding celebration from a digital device and the etiquette observed,  sort the Islamic and unislamic activities performed during wedding celebrations using flash cards,  role play the etiquette to be observed during the celebration e.g. (appropriate dressing, gender separation, avoiding Israaf and music) KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What are the Islamic etiquette that guides wedding celebrations? Core competences to be developed:  Communication and Collaboration: as learners brainstorm on a wedding celebration they have attended and note down what they observed/experienced  Critical thinking and problem solving: is enhanced as learners role play the etiquette to be observed during the celebration Values: Respect as learners brainstorm on a wedding celebration they have attended and note down what they observed/experienced PCIs:Responsibility as leaners role play the etiquette to be observed during the celebration and engages in assigned roles and duties Links to other subjects: The learner is able to relate to social organizations in Social Studies

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.0 Muamalat (Social Relations). SUB-STRAND: 6.2 Rights of Neighbours ( 2 Lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline the rights of neighbours for harmonious living, b) demonstrate the awareness of the rights of neighbours as an act of ibadah, c) appreciate the rights of neighbours as an obligatory act upon a Muslim. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  search the rights of neighbours in Islam using digital devices/print media and make notes,  Discuss in pairs/group the significance of treating neighbours well and display on a chart,  dramatize the right way of treating neighbours,  search for Hadith on the rights of neighbours and deduce lessons from it using digital devices/ books/resource persons. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How should Muslims relate with neighbours? 2. What are the significance of upholding good neighbourhood? Core competences to be developed:  Digital literacy: through searching for the rights of neighbours,  Critical thinking and problem solving: through dramatize the right way of treating neighbours Values: Love –caring for others as they dramatize the correct way of treating neighbours PCIs: Inter personal relations as they role-play/watch/ discuss in groups the rights of neighbours Links to other subjects: Social studies cover content on human rights Core competences to be developed:  Creativity and imagination: through undertake a project of creating a shop corner by collecting items, write a price list and a list of Islamic rules to be observed. Values: Responsibility as undertake a project of creating a shop corner by collecting items, write a price list and a list of Islamic rules to be observed PCIs: Financial literacy as they practise buying and selling and create a shop corner Links to other subjects: Mathematics covers related content. Core competences to be developed:  Digital literacy: the skill of interacting with digital technology as learners watch audio-visual clip on al-Isra wal Miraj from a digital device  Communication and collaboration: the skill of listening speaking and writing as learners discuss the importance of al-Isra wal Miraj in pairs or in groups and write the points in their notebook  Self efficacy: the skill of effective communication skills enhanced as learners read from reference material on the events of al-Isra wal Miraj individually and narrates it in class Values: Responsibility enhanced as learners discuss the major gift given to prophet (S.A.W) during al-Isra wal Miraj journey in pairs/groups and present in class PCIs: Self-esteem as learners narrate the Prophet’s miraculous journey to heaven. Links to other subjects: Social studies a learners discuss the means of transport used by the Prophet during the event.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 7.1 Pledges of Aqabah (Events that Led,Terms of Aqabah)
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.0 History of Islam. SUB-STRAND: 7.1 Pledges of Aqabah (Events that Led,Terms of Aqabah) (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) state the events that led to the signing of the pledges of Aqabah b) identify the terms of the pledges of Aqabah c) appreciate the pledges of Aqabah as a base for the migration of muslims in madina SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch a video on the pledges of Aqaba from a digital device and write the terms  discuss in group the events that led to the signing of the pledges of Aqabah  role play and present in class (e.g the Prophet (S.A.W) meeting delegates from Yathrib, preaching by Mus’ab bin Umayr in Madina, signing the pledges…) . KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is the pledges of Aqabah important in the History of Islam? 2. How did Muslims benefit from the pledges of Aqabah? Core competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration: through discussions in group on the events that led to the signing of the pledges of Aqabah  Creativity and imagination: as they learners role play role play and present in class (e.g the Prophet (S.A.W) meeting delegates from Yathrib, preaching by Mus’ab bin Umayr in Madina, signing the pledges…) Values: Unity-cooperation: as learners strive to achieve common goals by role play and present in class (e.g the Prophet (S.A.W) meeting delegates from Yathrib, preaching by Mus’ab bin Umayr in Madina, signing the pledges…) PCIs: Conflict resolution and negotiation as they discuss in group the events that led to the signing of the pledges of Aqabah Links to other subjects: social studies as of signing agreement is covered.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.0 History of Islam. SUB-STRAND: 7.3 Hijra to Madina (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) narrate the events on the Prophet’s migration to Madina, b) assess the significance of the Prophet (S.S.W)’s journey to Madina, c) appreciate the Prophet (S.A.W.)’s journey to Madina as milestone in islamic History. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen/watch a story on the Prophet (S.A.W.)’s migration to Madina from a digital device/teacher,  in group braistorm reasons for Prophets migration to Madina,  discuss the major events that took place during the Prophet (S.A.W.)’s migration to Madina e.g.(the Prophet (S.A.W) leaving Ali in his house ,departure with Abubakar, at cave Thaur, the incident of Suraqah,reception in Madina),  sing a Qasida of welcoming the Prophet (S.A.W) i.e Talaal Badru ‘alaynaa),  discuss the significance of Hijra and make short note e.g. end of persecution, unity of the Ummah, beginning of the Islamic calendar). KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why did the Prophet (S.A.W.) migrate to Madina? 2. Why is Hijra important to Muslims? Core competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration: as learners discuss the major events that took place during the Prophet (S.A.W.)’s migration to Madina e.g.(the Prophet (S.A.W) leaving Ali in his house ,departure with Abubakar, at cave Thaur, the incident of Suraqah,reception in Madina). Values: Patriotism-citizenship discuss the significance of Hijra and make short note e.g. end of persecution, unity of the Ummah, beginning of the Islamic calendar). PCIs: Leadership as they discuss the prophet in leadership in Madina which united people Links to other subjects: as learner discuss the migration from makkah to Madina,the learner is able to relate to movement of people in Social studies

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 7.4 Constitution of Madina ( Terms of Madina Constitution)
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.0 History of Islam. SUB-STRAND: 7.4 Constitution of Madina ( Terms of Madina Constitution) (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline the terms of Madina constitution, b) explain the importance of Madina constitution to the people of Madina, c) explain the role played by the Ansar in the settlement of Muhajirun in Madina, d) develop a desire to maintain Islamic brotherhood as per the teachings of Islam. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  brainstorm on the terms of Madina constitution ,  discuss in pairs/group the importance of Madina constituition to the people of Madina,  listen/watch a story on how united the Muhajirun and the Ansar were from a digital device/teacher,  discuss the role played by the Ansar in settling the Muhajirun (e.g. shared their wealth assisted them in integration and settlement),  discuss the lessons learnt from the spirit of brotherhood established by the Prophet (S.A.W) (Muslims must be united, assist one another). KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. why the was Madina constituition importance to the people of Madina? 2. What role did the Ansar play in the settlement of the Muhajirun? Core competences to be developed:  Communication and collaboration: through discussion on the lessons learnt from the spirit of brotherhood established by the Prophet (s.a.w) (Muslims must be united, assist one another) Values: Peace, love and unity as the learners discuss the importance of Madina constitution to the people of Madina in conflict resolution PCIs: Good governance as they discuss the importance of Madina constitution to the people of Madina Links to other subjects: social studies in teaching cohesion Suggested Resources Prophets after class, games, sports and participate in good leadership in school -Narrates stories of prophets during free time to other learners

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 1.1.1 Matamshi Bora (Vipindi 4). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua silabi zinazotokana na sauti zinazokaribiana katika maneno: f/v, s/z, l/r na th/dh, b) kutamka silabi zinazotokana na sauti zinazokaribiana kimatamshi: f/v, s/z, l/r na th/dh ili kutofautisha matamshi yake, c) kutamka vitanzandimi vinavyoundwa SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua silabi za sauti lengwa kutokana na maneno kwenye vitabu, ubaoni au kwa kutumia vifaa vya kiteknolojia,  kusikiliza silabi za sauti f/v, s/z, l/r/ na th/dh zikitamkwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kutoka kwa vifaa vya kiteknolojia (k.v. kinasasauti),  kutamka silabi za sauti lengwa akiwa na wenzake,  kusikiliza vitanzandimi vinavyoundwa kutokana na maneno yenye sauti lengwa vikikaririwa (k.m. shirika la reli la Rwanda larejelea shughuli zake rasmi),  kuunda vitanzandimi vinavyotokana na sauti KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Je, unajua maneno gani yenye silabi zinazokangany a kimatamshi? 2. Je, unajua vitanzandimi gani vyenye silabi zinazokangany a kimatamshi? kwa silabi za sauti zinazokaribiana kimatamshi: f/v, s/z, l/r na th/dh ili kuimarisha mawasiliano, d) kuunda vitanzandimi vyenye maana kutokana na sauti zinazokaribiana kimatamshi: f/v, s/z, l/r na th/dh ) e) kuchangamkia kukariri vitanzandimi vinavyoundwa kwa silabi za sauti zinazokaribiana kimatamshi: f/v, s/z, l/r na th/dh) ili kuimarisha matamshi yake. husika akiwa peke yake, wawiliwawili au katika vikundi,  kuunda vitanzandimi kwenye vifaa vya kidijitali na kushirikiana na wenzake mitamboni kuvirekebisha,  kusakura mtandaoni ili kupata vitanzandimi zaidi vyenye sauti lengwa. Umilisi wa Kimsingi Unaokuzwa  Mawasiliano na ushirikiano – wanafunzi wanaposhirikiana katika kutamka silabi na kuunda vitanzandimi.  Ujuzi wa kidijitali – wakati vifaa vya kiteknolojia vinapotumiwa kusikiliza sauti na kuunda vitanzandimi mtandaoni.  Hamu ya ujifunzaji – mwanafunzi anapoendelea kukariri vitanzandimi na kusakura mtandaoni ili kupata vitanzandimi zaidi.  Ubunifu – mwanafunzi anapounda vitanzandimi vyenye maana.  Kujiamini - mwanafunzi anapotamka kwa usahihi silabi zinazotokana na sauti lengwa na kuunda vitanzandimi sahihi.  Uwazaji kina na utatuzi wa matatizo –mwanafunzi anapofikiria kuhusu vitanzandimi atakavyounda vyenye sauti lengwa. Maadili  Umoja– mwanafunzi anapofanya kazi katika vikundi.  Uwajibikaji-mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika shughuli za kikundi na kutumia vifaa vya kikundi. Masuala Mtambuko  Masuala mtambuko anuwai kutokana na vitanzandimi vinavyoelekeza utoaji wa maelezo kuhusu masuala hayo k.v. utunzaji wa mazingira, ujuzi wa matumizi ya fedha, afya bora na utunzaji wa wanyama.  Kujithamini-mwanafunzi anapounda na kutamka vitanzandimi vilivyo na sauti lengwa. Uhusiano na Masomo Mengine English, Indigenous Languages– Matamshi bora pia hufundishwa katika masomo hayo.

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.2 Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 1.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufahamu (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa uliotumika katika kifungu ili kuimarisha ufahamu, b) kutumia msamiati lengwa kwa usahihi katika sentensi, c) kusoma kifungu cha hadithi kwa kuzingatia ujumbe, matukio na wahusika, d) kuonyesha uelewa SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa (k.v. vyakula, viungo vya kupikia, njia za kupika na vifaa vya kupikia) kwa kutumia kadi za maneno, chati, mti maneno au kifaa cha kidijitali,  kushiriki katika vikundi kujadili na kutumia msamiati wa suala lengwa katika sentensi,  kusoma kifungu kuhusu suala lengwa kwenye kitabu au kwenye tarakilishi akiwa peke yake, wawiliwawili au katika vikundi,  kutoa muhtasari kuhusu kifungu alichosoma,  kujibu maswali kutokana na kifungu alichosoma, kusoma vifungu mtandaoni kuhusu KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Kusoma kuhusu mapishi kuna umuhimu gani? 2. Ni hadithi gani umewahi kuisoma kuhusu mapishi? wa kifungu kwa kutoa muhtasari na kujibu maswali, kujenga mazoea ya usomaji bora katika maisha ya kila siku. suala lengwa na kujadiliana na wenzake kuhusu ujumbe ulioyomo. Umilisi wa Kimsingi Unaokuzwa  Mawasiliano na ushirikiano - mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika mijadala na kazi za vikundi.  Ujuzi wa kidijitali - wakati vifaa vya kidijitali vinapotumiwa kusoma kifungu.  Hamu ya ujifunzaji - mwanafunzi anaposakura mtandaoni ili kusoma vifungu zaidi kuhusu suala lengwa. Maadili  Umoja – mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika shughuli za vikundi.  Heshima-mwanafunzi anapoziheshimu kazi za wenzake kwenye kikundi. Masuala Mtambuko  Masuala ya afya -mwanfunzi anapojifunza kuhusu mapishi.  Afya ya mtu binafsi – mwanafunzi anaposoma vifungu vinavyoeleza kuhusu mapishi. Uhusiano na Masomo Mengine English, Indigenous Language – masomo haya .hushughulikia vifungu vya hadithi na upanuzi wa msamiati.

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 1.3.1 Insha ya wasifu (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua insha ya wasifu kwa kuzingatia mtindo na muundo wake, b) kuandika insha ya wasifu kwa ubunifu ili kujenga maelezo yenye kutoa picha dhahiri, c) kufurahia kutunga insha bora ili kuimarisha mazoea ya kuandika. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua insha ya wasifu kwa kurejelea vielelezo vya insha zilizoandikwa kwenye matini mbalimbali au tarakilishi,  kusoma vielelezo vya insha ya wasifu vilivyoandikwa katika matini mbalimbali au tarakilishi,  kushirikiana na wenzake kujadili mada na muundo wa insha ya wasifu,  kukishirikiana na wenzake katika vikundi ili kubainisha na kujadili vidokezo vifaavyo vya mada lengwa,  kuaandika insha ya wasifu isiyopungua maneno 150 inayohusu mada lengwa (k.v. Mpishi nimpendaye) kwa kuzingatia, anwani, mpangilio mzuri wa mawazo, hati safi, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Insha ya wasifu inahusu nini? 2. Unazingatia nini unapoandika insha ya wasifu? kanuni za kisarufi (k.v uakifishaji mwafaka na tahajia) na kwa lugha ya kiubunifu inayojumuisha methali, tashbihi na nahau alizojifunza awali,  kuandika insha ya wasifu mtandaoni na kuisambaza kwa wenzake na mwalimu ili kuisoma na kuitathmini,  kuwasomea wenzake insha aliyoandika ili kumpa motisha kuandika zaidi. kumwonyesha mzazi au mlezi wake insha ya wasifu aliyoandika ili apate maoni. Umilisi wa Kimsingi Unaokuzwa  Mawasiliano na ushirikiano – unakuzwa mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika mijadala na kazi za vikundi.  Ujuzi wa kidijitali – unakuzwa wakati vifaa vya kidijitali vinapotumiwa kuandika insha mtandaoni na kurejelea kielelezo cha insha ya wasifu.  Ubunifu – mwanafunzi anapoandika insha ya wasifu. Maadili  Heshima na adabu - hasa katika shughuli za vikundi.  Insha ya wasifu yaweza kulenga watu ambao wanajulikana kwa uadilifu, uwajibikaji, upendo na uzalendo. Masuala Mtambuko Elimu ya afya na kujikinga –mwanafunzi anapofanya kazi pamoja na wenzake katika vikundi anajifunza mambo ya afya. Uhusiano na Masomo Mengine English na Indigenous Languages – Masomo haya yanashughulika mada ya kuandika.

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 1.4.1 Nomino za Pekee (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua nomino za pekee kwenye sentensi au vifungu vya maneno, b) kutunga sentensi kwa kutumia nomino za pekee ili kukuza matumizi ya lugha sahihi, c) kuchangamkia matumizi ya nomino za pekee katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua nomino za pekee (k.v. Kisumu, Mei, Rabuka, Alhamisi na Yohana) kwenye tarakilishi, kapu maneno, mti maneno, kadi maneno au chati,  kutaja nomino za pekee akiwa na wenzake kama vile za majina ya mji, majina ya mito, majina ya watu na majina ya miezi,  kutambua nomino za pekee katika sentensi kwenye vitabu, tarakilishi, chati kwa kuzipigia mstari au kukolezea rangi,  kujaza nafasi kwenye sentensi au kifungu kwa kutumia nomino za pekee,  kutunga sentensi kwa kutumia nomino za pekee akiwa na wenzake. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Nomino za pekee zinahusu nini? 2. Ni nomino zipi za pekee unazozijua? Umilisi wa Kimsingi Unaokuzwa  Mawasiliano na ushirikiano - mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika kazi za vikundi.  Ujuzi wa kidijitali - wakati vifaa vya kiteknolojia vinapotumiwa katika kutambua nomino za pekee.  Ubunifu - mwanafunzi anapotunga sentensi sahihi akitumia nomino za pekee.  Kujiamini - mwanafunzi anapofaulu kutambua nomino za pekee na kuzitungia sentensi sahihi. Maadili  Uwajibikaji- mwanafunzi anapofanya kazi ya darasani.  Uzalendo na heshima- mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake na kuheshimu maoni ya wengine.  Maadili mbalimbali yanaweza kulengwa katika sentensi k.v. upendo, uaminifu, uzalendo, amani na umoja. Masuala Mtambuko Masuala mtambuko anuwai kutokana na sentensi zinazoelekeza utoaji wa maelezo kuhusu masuala hayo k.v. usalama, utunzaji wa mazingira, afya bora na utunzaji wa wanyama. Uhusiano na Masomo Mengine English na Indigenous Languages – masomo haya yanashughulikia mada ya nomino

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 1.4.2 Nomino za kawaida (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua nomino za kawaida kwenye sentensi au vifungu vya maneno, b) kutunga sentensi kwa kutumia nomino za kawaida ili kukuza matumizi sahihi ya lugha, c) kufurahia kutumia nomino za kawaida katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua nomino za kawaida kwenye kadi au kapu la maneno (k.v.mtu, mtoto, darasa, ukuta, mwalimu, meza na kiti),  kutaja akiwa na wenzake nomino za kawaida,  kutambua nomino za kawaida katika sentensi kwa kuzipigia mistari au kuzikolezea rangi kwenye tarakilishi,  kutumia nomino za kawaida kujaza nafasi kwenye sentensi,  kutunga sentensi kwa kutumia nomino za kawaida akiwa peke yake wawiliwawili au kwenye vikundi. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Je, ni vitu gani vipatikanavyo katika mazingira yako? 2. Ni vitu gani vinavyotumi wa katika mapishi mbalimbali? Umilisi wa Kimsingi Unaokuzwa  Ubunifu- anapotunga sentensi na kujaza nafasi.  Mawasiliano na ushirikiano- mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika vikundi kutaja nomino na kutunga sentensi. Maadili  Upendo - mwanafunzi anapotagamana na wenzake kwenye vikundi.  Heshima - mwanafunzi anapothamini maoni ya wengine kwenye kikundi.  Maadili mbalimbali yanaweza kulengwa katika sentensi k.v. upendo, uaminifu, uzalendo, amani na umoja. Masuala Mtambuko  Mshikamano wa kijamii na utaifa - hasa unatokea kwenye kazi za vikundi wakati mwanafunzi anashirikiana na wenzake.  Masuala mtambuko anuwai kutokana na sentensi zinazotoa maelezo kuhusu masuala hayo k.v. utunzaji wa mazingira, afya bora na utunzaji wa wanyama. Uhusiano na Masomo Mengine English na Indigenous Languages - masomo haya yanashughulikia mada ya nomino.

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 2.1.1 Maamkuzi na Maagano (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua aina mbalimbali za maamkuzi na maagano katika mawasiliano, b) kueleza maamkuzi na maagano yanayotumik katika miktadha mbalimbali ili kuyabainisha, c) kutumia aina mbalimbali za maamkuzi na maagano katika mawasiliano, d) kuchangamkia maamkuzi na SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua maamkuzi (k.v. shikamoo, Habari za utokako? Habari za adhuhuri? Habari za jioni?) kutoka kwenye chati, ubao au vifaa vya kidijitali, michoro na picha,  kushiriki kujadiliana na mwenzake a au katika vikundi maamkuzi yanayolengwa na matumizi yake,  kutambua maagano (k.v lala salama, safari njema, alamsiki) kutoka kwenye chati, ubao au vifaa vya kidijitali, michoro na picha,  kushirikiana na wenzake kuigiza maamkuzi na maagano lengwa,  ktazama watu wakiamkuana na kuagana katika vifaa vya kidijitali, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Je, watu husalimiana vipi katika jamii? 2. Je, watu huagana vipi katika jamii? maagano katika mahusiano.  kuambatanisha maamkuzi na maagano na majibu sahihi. Umilisi wa Kimsingi Unaokuzwa  Mawasiliano na ushirikiano- mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kuigiza maamkuzi na maagano.  Ujuzi wa kidijitali- mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kujifunzia.  Kujiamini- mwanafunzi anapotumia maamkuzi na maagano ipasavyo. Masuala Mtambuko  Utunzi na usalama wa watoto –mwanafunzi anapoamkua na kujibu maamkuzi.  Utangamano wa kijamii-mwanafunzi anapoamkuana na kuagana na wenzake . Uhusiano na Masomo Mengine English na Indigenous Languages - masomo haya yanashughlikia maamkuzi na maagano.

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.text: STRAND: Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 2.2.1 Kusoma kwa Kina (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua mpangilio wa maneno katika kamusi ili kupata maneno lengwa kwa urahisi, b) kutumia kamusi ipasavyo kutafuta maana za maneno asiyoyajua yaliyo katika matini teule ili kukuza msamiati wake, c) kuchangamkia kutumia kamusi katika kukuza msamiati wake. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kupanga maneno aliyopewa kwenye chati, kapu maneno au mti maneno kialfabeti,  kuchague neno kutoka kapu maneno au mti maneno ili kulitafuta kwenye kamusi,  kutumia kamusi kutafuta maana za maneno mbalimbali akiwa peke yake, wawiliwawili au katika vikundi,  kutumia mtandao kutafuta maana za maneno. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Maana ya maneno ya Kiswahili hupatikana wapi? Umilisi wa Kimsingi Unaokuzwa  Mawasiliano na ushirikiano - mwanafunzi anashirikiana na wenzake kutafuta maana za maneno.  Ujuzi wa kidijitali - mwanafunzi anatumia mtandao kutafuta maana za maneno.  Kujiamini-mwanafunzi anapotumia kamusi kutafutamaana ya maneno.  Hamu ya ujifunzaji - mwanafunzi anapoanza kutumia kamusi kutafuta maana za maneno. Masuala Mtambuko  Uwajibikaji – mwanafunzi anapokuwa na uwezo wa kujitegemea katika kutumia kamusi.  Kujithamini –mwanafunzi anapofanya kazi na wengine katika vikundi.  Masuala ya afya-mwanafunzi anaposoma kifungu kuhusu huduma ya kwanza. Uhusiano na Masomo Mengine English na Indigenous Languages – masomo haya husisitiza matumizi mbalimbali ya kamusi.

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 2.3.1 Insha ya masimulizi (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua insha ya masimulizi kwa kuzingatia ujumbe, mtindo na muundo, b) kuandika insha ya masimulizi kwa kufuata kanuni zifaazo, c) kuchangamkia utunzi mzuri wa insha ya masimulizi ili kukuza ubunifu wake. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua insha ya masimulizi kwa kurejelea vielelezo vya insha zilizoandikwa kwenye matini mbalimbali au tarakilishi,  kushiriki na wenzake kujadili mada ya insha na muundo wa insha ya masimulizi,  kuandika insha isiyopungua maneno 150 inayosimulia kisa cha tukio linalohusiana na huduma ya kwanza kwa kuzingatia anwani, mpangilio mzuri wa mawazo, hati safi, tahajia, kanuni za kisarufi, uakifishaji mwafaka na kwa lugha ya kiubunifu,  kuandika insha ya masimulizi mtandaoni na kuisambaza kwa wenzake na mwalimu ili kuisoma na kuitathmini, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, unazingatia nini ili kuandika insha nzuri ya masimulizi?  kusomea wenzake insha aliyoandika ili kuitathmini. Umilisi wa Kimsingi Unaokuzwa  Mawasiliano na ushirikiano – unakuzwa wanafunzi wanaposhiriki katika mijadala na kazi za vikundi.  Ujuzi wa kidijitali – unakuzwa wakati vifaa vya kiteknolojia vinapotumiwa kuandika insha mtandaoni na kurejelea kielelezo cha insha ya masimulizi.  Ubunifu – unajengeka mwanafunzi anapoandika insha ya masimulizi.  Hamu ya ujifunzaji – unakuzwa mwanafunzi anapoimarisha ujuzi wake wa kutumia tarakilishi. Maadili  Heshima na adabu hasa katika shughuli za vikundi.  Umoja – mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika shughuli za vikundi. Masuala Mtambuko  Mshikamano wa kijamii na utaifa- mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kufanya kazi.  Masuala ya afya-mwanafunzi anapoandika insha kuhusu huduma ya kwanza. Uhusiano na Masomo Mengine English na Indigenous Language – masomo haya yanashughulikia uandishi wa insha

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 2.4.1 Nomino za Wingi (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze; a) kutambua nomino za wingi katika matini ili kuzibainisha, b) kutumia nomino za wingi katika sentensi ili kuimarisha mawasiliano, c) kufurahia kutumia nomino za wingi katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi  kutambua nomino za wingi (k.m chumvi, sukari, maji, uji, mafuta na manukato) kutoka kwenye kapu la maneno, chati, vitabu na vifaa vya kidijitali akiwa peke yake, wawiliwawili au katika kikundi,  kutambua nomino za wingi kwa kuzipigia mistari au kuzikolezea rangi kwenye matini,  kutumia nomino za wingi kujaza nafasi kwenye sentensi,  kutumia nomino za wingi katika sentensi kwa kufanya mazoezi daftarini. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Unajua majina gani yanayohusu vitu vinavyopatikana katika wingi tu? Umilisi wa Kimsingi Unaokuzwa  Mawasiliano na ushirikiano - mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika mijadala na kazi za vikundi.  Kufikiri kwa kina – anapotunga sentensi na kuzijadili na wenzake.  Ujuzi wa kidijitali - wakati vifaa vya kiteknolojia vinapotumiwa katika kutambua nomino za wingi. Maadili  Upendo – Unakuzwa anaposhiriki kwenye vikundi.  Uwajibikaji – Anawajibika kukamilisha kazi zake pamoja na kutunza vifaa vya kidijitali kama vile tarakalishi. Masuala Mtambuko  Utangamano wakijamii – anaposhirikiana na wenzake kwenye kikundi.  Kujithamini – anapokuza stadi ya kujieleza kupitia utungaji wa sentensi. Uhusiano na Masomo Mengine English na Indigenous Languages – masomo haya yanafunza nomino.

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 2.4.2 Vitenzi-jina (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze; a) kutambua nomino za vitenzi-jina kwenye kifungu cha maneno au kwenye sentensi, b) kutunga sentensi au vifungu vya maneno akitumia nomino za vitenzi- jina ili kukuza matumizi bora ya lugha, c) kufurahia kutumia nomino za vitenzi- jina katika utungaji wa sentensi na kujaza nafasi. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua vitenzi-jina kutoka kwenye kapu la maneno, vyombo vya kijiditali (k.v. kusoma, kucheka, kula, kulia na kuandika.),  kutambua vitenzi-jina akiwa na wenzake kwa kuvipigia mistari au kuzikolezea rangi kwenye matini n.k,  kutumia nomino za vitenzi- jina kwa kujaza nafasi kwenye sentensi,  kutunga sentensi au vifungu vya maneno kwa kutumia nomino za vitenzi-jina akiwa peke yake, wawiliwawili au katika vikundi.
